service: Hospital beds for home use (including variable height and electric adjustment features)
vignette: 77-year-old man with severe COPD (ICD-10-CM J44.9, FEV1 28% predicted) and orthopnea. He becomes acutely short of breath within minutes of lying flat and must sleep every night with his head and trunk elevated at least 30-45 degrees; pillows and a foam wedge in his ordinary bed slide out of position and have not worked. The physician's prescription, submitted with the initial claim, names the COPD, describes nightly orthopnea with desaturation to 85% when flat, and orders a manual (crank-adjusted) hospital bed for positioning.
rationale_note: COPD requiring nightly head elevation not achievable with pillows; prescription states condition, severity, frequency.

service: Hospital beds for home use (including variable height and electric adjustment features)
vignette: 69-year-old woman recovering at home from a cervical spine injury who requires continuous cervical traction in bed for 6 weeks. The traction apparatus mounts on a bed frame and the supplier documents that it cannot be fixed to or used on her ordinary bed. The physician's prescription, submitted with the initial claim, describes the cervical injury and specifies the traction frame attachment that requires a hospital bed, and orders a manual hospital bed.
rationale_note: Special attachment that cannot be used on an ordinary bed; prescription names the condition and the attachment.

service: Hospital beds for home use (including variable height and electric adjustment features)
vignette: 84-year-old woman with mild knee osteoarthritis who sleeps comfortably flat in her ordinary bed and needs no special positioning or attachments. Her daughter requests a hospital bed because it would make it easier for her mother to get in and out of bed and easier for the daughter to change the sheets. The physician's prescription, submitted with the claim, states 'osteoarthritis of knees, hospital bed for convenience of transfers and care.'
rationale_note: No positioning need or attachment; requested for ease of getting in and out of bed and caregiver convenience.

service: Hospital beds for home use (including variable height and electric adjustment features)
vignette: 81-year-old man with congestive heart failure. The physician's prescription, submitted with the initial claim, reads 'Hospital bed. Diagnosis: CHF. Patient requires positioning.' No other documentation is submitted; the record does not describe his symptoms, how severe they are, or how often they occur.
rationale_note: Positioning need stated with a diagnosis, but no severity or frequency of symptoms anywhere in the documentation.

service: Hospital beds for home use (including variable height and electric adjustment features)
vignette: 79-year-old woman with severe rheumatoid arthritis who already has a covered manual hospital bed for positioning to relieve joint pain. She now needs frequent position changes through the night. She has fixed ulnar deviation and flexion contractures of all fingers and cannot press or hold any bed control; her husband would operate the controls for her. She has no spinal cord injury and no brain injury or other neurologic disease. The supplier requests coverage of electric powered head and foot adjustments.
rationale_note: Patient cannot operate the controls and has neither spinal cord injury nor brain damage, so the exception does not apply.

service: Hospital beds for home use (including variable height and electric adjustment features)
vignette: 72-year-old man with severe heart failure (LVEF 20%) who already has a covered hospital bed for positioning. He has episodes of paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea 3-4 nights per week in which he wakes gasping and must be upright immediately; turning the manual crank or waiting for help takes several minutes and has led to two emergency calls. He has normal hand function and can operate a bed control pendant himself. The physician documents the condition, the frequency and severity of the episodes, and that no delay in repositioning can be tolerated. The supplier requests coverage of electric powered head and foot adjustments.
rationale_note: Electric adjustments: immediate need for position change (no delay tolerated) and the patient can operate the controls.

service: Hospital beds for home use (including variable height and electric adjustment features)
vignette: 74-year-old woman with COPD who has a covered manual hospital bed for nightly head elevation. Her positioning need is unchanged all night: the head of the bed is raised once at bedtime and lowered once in the morning, and she has no episodes requiring urgent repositioning. She can operate controls. She would prefer electric controls because the hand crank is tiring for her husband. The supplier requests coverage of electric powered head and foot adjustments.
rationale_note: Positioning is needed once nightly with no frequent or immediate need; electric adjustment is a convenience.

service: Hospital beds for home use (including variable height and electric adjustment features)
vignette: 88-year-old man with end-stage dementia who is completely bedbound, does not sit on the edge of the bed, does not stand, ambulate, or transfer to a chair or wheelchair, and has no cardiac disease. He has a covered manual hospital bed for positioning to prevent contractures. His caregiver requests a variable height feature so the bed can be raised to make bathing him easier on her back.
rationale_note: Bedbound patient who neither ambulates nor transfers; variable height matches none of the listed conditions.

service: Hospital beds for home use (including variable height and electric adjustment features)
vignette: 67-year-old man with C6 quadriplegia who must be repositioned every 2 hours, around the clock, with his body aligned in ways an ordinary bed cannot provide, to prevent contractures and pressure injuries. Home-health nursing notes describing his condition and repositioning schedule are attached to the supplier's initial claim for a manual hospital bed. No physician's prescription is included with the claim or anywhere in the submitted records.
rationale_note: Clinical need appears met, but no physician's prescription accompanies the initial claim.

service: Hospital beds for home use (including variable height and electric adjustment features)
vignette: 58-year-old woman on Medicare through disability with C5 quadriplegia from a diving injury. She must be repositioned every 2 hours day and night with specific trunk and limb alignment and periodic head elevation to prevent contractures, pressure injuries, and aspiration pneumonia; this cannot be done in her ordinary bed. She cannot use her hands, and her caregivers do all repositioning. The physician's prescription, submitted with the initial claim, describes the quadriplegia, the repositioning frequency, and the severity of her contracture and aspiration risk, and orders a manual hospital bed.
rationale_note: Quadriplegia with positioning every 2 hours; documented. The patient's inability to operate controls is irrelevant for a manual bed.
